title: Microsoft Teams: add SharePoint agents to chats from the in-context store
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents how SharePoint agents handle Teams chats whose members have different permissions, but the briefing says this is unknown. The requesting user can review and share an answer that other chat members could not access directly, an important qualification for the data-exposure assessment.

claims.claim: The general tenant-level Teams app control is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams documents Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> for changing the tenant app state, without establishing a reliable Boolean direction in its examples.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The Teams discovery feature is enabled by default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Mixed licensing and variable cost reflect Copilot licence access or metered SharePoint-agent pay-as-you-go access.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The notice asks for E3 or E5 with Teams and either Microsoft 365 Copilot or pay-as-you-go separately configured for SharePoint agents on Mac.
claims.quote: Ensure that intended users have E3 or E5 (with Teams) licensing, and one of the following options: - Microsoft 365 Copilot license OR- Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) separately setup for SharePoint agents on MAC.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot licence assignment is a documented route to SharePoint-agent access.
claims.quote: Currently, users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use the agents.

claims.claim: For pay-as-you-go users without a Copilot licence, access is controlled through the security group assigned to the billing policy.
claims.quote: For users who aren't assigned with a Microsoft Copilot license, you can control user access to agents through pay-as-you-go billing. ... Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing helpdesk staff about SharePoint-agent access and usage questions.
claims.quote: Inform helpdesk staff in case users have questions about accessing or using SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for this in-context-store discovery capability.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams in-context store Add Agents and Bots; "SharePoint agents" "in-context". Opened manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and training/modules/use-no-code-agents-sharepoint/3-share-agent-microsoft-teams; neither documents this discovery entry point.

claims.claim: In SharePoint, an agent's responses to a user exclude sources that user cannot access.
claims.quote: if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: differing data-source permissions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how SharePoint-agent responses are handled in a Teams chat whose members have different source permissions.
claims.quote: If the user who asks the question has permission to see the answer, but some members in the chat group don't, the user sees a message explaining that the answer can't be automatically added to the chat.
claims.fix: Replace the shared-chat uncertainty in Data exposure and remove the corresponding Open question. Write: "In Teams, the agent checks the requesting user's permissions. If other chat members lack access, the answer is not posted automatically: the requester can select View response, review it, and decide whether to share it with the group." Cite and add to sources https://support.microsoft.com/office/share-an-agent-from-sharepoint-in-teams-6dcbf7b5-8c13-44e5-a68a-dbd71fb76ad3.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted content discovery removes the Agent icon and turns off agent-related features on the flagged SharePoint site.
claims.quote: you can turn off all agent-related features on individual sites by using the restricted content discovery feature. Once you flag a site with restricted content discovery, users can't see the Agent icon on the global header of the site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted content discovery prevents adding the flagged site's content to other agents.
claims.quote: they don't have access to use the ready-made agent, create new agents, or add content from that site to any other agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: The notice and feature-specific documentation do not establish actions beyond answering for agents discovered through this entry point.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams shared chat responses permissions actions; "SharePoint" "agents" "Teams" "actions" "permissions". Opened MC1193415, Teams sharing Support guidance and Learn training on sharing agents; no action mechanism specific to the in-context store is documented.

claims.claim: Users without either a Copilot licence or pay-as-you-go access may be unable to use discovered agents.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center currently affects Copilot Chat, not Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents 12 messages for a SharePoint-agent interaction responding to a single complex prompt.
claims.quote: each interaction with a SharePoint agent uses 12 messages (10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from the user.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding accounts for 10 messages in that interaction.
claims.quote: 10 messages for tenant graph grounding

claims.claim: Generative answers account for 2 messages in that interaction.
claims.quote: 2 messages for generative answers

claims.claim: SharePoint-agent usage charges appear under the Copilot Studio invoice meter.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services is included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.claim: A budget can be created in Microsoft Cost Management under Monitoring > Budgets.
claims.quote: You can quickly create a budget under Monitoring > Budgets for your selected scope.

claims.claim: The SharePoint-agent Azure billing resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot licence uses an agent.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: The published pay-as-you-go rate for agents in SharePoint is USD $0.01 per message.
claims.quote: | Agents in SharePoint | The number of messages used. | $0.01/message |

claims.claim: Learn names a SharePoint administrator among the prerequisites for setting up SharePoint agents as an Azure resource.
claims.quote: To set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure, you need to have at least the following permissions as: - A SharePoint administrator

claims.claim: Owner or Contributor Azure roles are needed on the subscription and linked resource group during billing setup.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure subscription ... Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure resource group linked to the same Azure subscription ... You only need the Owner or Contributor Azure roles during the billing setup process.

claims.claim: The SharePoint billing page gives Copilot > Billing and usage, while its linked setup guide instead gives Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost management . In the banner at the top of the dashboard, select Classic Billing & usage.

claims.claim: The Teams app-management guidance names the Teams Administrator role for using the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Admins can turn Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint on or off per user in the Copilot licence's service plans.
claims.quote: Under the license details page for Microsoft Copilot on the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can turn 'Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint' on or off on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: Disabling that service plan also disables Copilot in OneDrive and SharePoint page authoring for that user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically confirmed Manage apps or a policy hiding Add Agents and Bots for SharePoint agents in the in-context store.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams in-context store admin control policy hide Add Agents and Bots. Opened microsoftteams/manage-apps and sharepoint/manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint; reviewed agent-settings and agent-actions search excerpts; no specific mapping or hiding policy found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Cost Management can show a SharePoint-agent consumption breakdown beneath the invoiced Copilot Studio usage.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice. However, in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes an -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking, justifying the briefing's warning against relying on its Boolean direction.
